notes:
The one scripture beat was painted JESUS-RED. Exodus is Old Testament, so it
cannot be red - and it is the LORD speaking in first person, which makes it
GREEN, not blue:
  s1  Exodus 25:8  'And let them make me a sanctuary; that I may dwell
                    among them.'                                   RED -> GOD
'Make ME a sanctuary, that I may dwell among them' - that is Jehovah, the
premortal Christ, talking about himself. Straightforward green.

NO SPLIT on s1. The whole segment is Deity's own words with no narrator clause
attached; Moses's 'And the LORD spake unto Moses, saying' is not in this
segment, so there is nothing to peel off.

LIFTED ONE VERSE out of narrator paraphrase:
  g22  Exodus 25:22  'And there I will meet with thee, and I will commune
                      with thee from above the mercy seat...'      NEW, god
n2a already listed the ark and the table and the lampstand, and n2b already said
'every detail meant to say: I am near' - but the viewer never heard God actually
say it. Exodus 25:22 is that sentence, in his own first person, and it is the
warmest line in the chapter. Quoted through 'the ark of the testimony' - a clean
clause boundary mid-verse, verbatim to that point, the same way the reference
plan handles Genesis 18:32a. g22 sits on S3 with n2a so no artwork changes.

ADDED two narrator retellings, both required by the retelling rule:
  n0b  retells Exodus 25:8 immediately after it, on S2 with s1.
  n2r  retells Exodus 25:22 immediately after it, on S4 with n2b.
Before this, s1's Old English had to wait until n1a/n1b - four beats later - for
any plain-English landing.

Nothing left as paraphrase from uncertainty.

WHY-LAW: milk. God asked for a tent, not a fortress, and he asked for it in the
middle of the camp. The whole point is nearness - he wanted to live where his
people lived. Nothing on screen argues about temples; the tent says it.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: While Israel camped in the wilderness, the LORD gave Moses a strange instruction — have the people build me a sanctuary.

segments.speaker: god
segments.text: And let them make me a sanctuary; that I may dwell among them.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Build me a place, God said, so that I can live right there with you. Not a palace on a far-off hill. A tent, pitched in the middle of the camp, with everybody else's tents circled around it.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He told them exactly how — the ark, the table, the lampstand —

segments.speaker: god
segments.text: And there I will meet with thee, and I will commune with thee from above the mercy seat, from between the two cherubims which are upon the ark of the testimony.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: That is what all the measurements were for. There, God said — right there, above that lid, between those two carved angels — that is where I will meet you and talk with you. He gave them an address.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: every detail meant to say: I am near.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Not for his sake. For theirs.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So that he could dwell among them in the middle of their ordinary days.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The pattern was carried by a people on the move,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: yet the promise was fixed — God with his people.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Centuries later that promise would take a face. But here it begins as a tent in the desert, God pitching his tent beside them.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He wanted to live among his people then. He wants to live among you now.

stills_wanted.S2: S2 now carries God's own words in green and then the storyteller in white. Frame the moment of the instruction being given rather than Moses as a figure: the mountain top, the man small in it, and the camp far below in the valley - because the whole sentence is about God wanting to come DOWN there. The valley should read as the destination, not the backdrop.
stills_wanted.S3: S3 now carries two beats and the caption turns white to green on it - the storyteller listing the furnishings, then God himself naming the meeting place. It needs to hold the mercy seat specifically: the lid of the ark with the two cherubim facing each other, and the empty space between them where the voice is promised. Light in that gap, nothing in it. The point of the beat is that God gave them a spot, so the spot has to be legible.
stills_wanted.S4: S4 now carries two beats of narration back to back. Pull back from the object to the people: craftsmen at work on the pieces, heads down, ordinary hands doing sacred work. Warm and unhurried. It should feel like a promise being built, not a ritual being performed.
